artboards: 00-system-sheet (row anatomy inside the list-row example, timeline cell)
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' #sys, the list-row example's timeline cell (5 dots: passed, passed, next, ahead, ahead); README.md §0.4 'Meters and timeline on every row' and 'Passed = filled green dot; next = larger dot in the item's band colour with a ring, ahead = hollow'
notes: The fixture (2 past, 1 current, 2 future entries) reproduces the artboard row example's own dot pattern (2 passed, 1 next, 2 ahead) so the artboard's own numbers are the comparison.

The artboard's track is 2px tall, green from 0 to the 'next' dot's position (58%) then rgba(0,0,0,.12) beyond. The built component renders a single 1px rgba(0,0,0,.12) line with no green portion at all — read this as a real geometry/colour gap, not a harness artefact: MilestoneTimeline.tsx's own track span has one style object, no conditional green segment.

The artboard places dots at fixed pixel offsets (0, 24, 42, 58, 76px) within the 76px cell; the built component uses `justify-content:space-between` across a `width:100%` row, which auto-spaces n dots evenly rather than at those exact offsets. Position is not asserted below (space-between vs fixed-px is a layout-strategy difference the harness cannot fairly reduce to one number for n dots); the dot SIZES and COLOURS are asserted, which is where the fixed vocabulary lives.

Selectors reach dots by DOM order: MilestoneTimeline.tsx has no per-dot marker class, so nth-of-type addresses the classifier's output directly (dot 1/2 = passed, dot 3 = next, dot 4/5 = ahead, per milestone-timeline-classify.ts, proven independently by its own npmtest.mjs).

children.note: dc.html #sys: height 2px, green 0-58%, rgba(0,0,0,.12) beyond. Built: height 1px, flat rgba(0,0,0,.12) throughout (no green segment) — logged as the comparison; only the built value's own baseline colour/height is asserted here since the split-gradient has no single computed-style equivalent.

children.name: dot 3 — next (band colour, ring)
children.note: dc.html #sys: 8x8px, background is the band colour (#F97316 in the artboard's own example, matching this fixture's Action band), box-shadow ring (artboard: '0 0 0 2px #fff' — a white ring; the built component's ring is the band colour at 20% alpha, '0 0 0 2px <bandHex>33' — a real colour divergence, logged as the comparison). Built dot size is 9x9px, not 8x8px.
